description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs:196-205

```rust
/// Add a pre-existing node to an account (used to set up test
/// fixtures).
///
/// The state counter is NOT incremented — this is silent fixture
/// setup.
pub fn seed_node(&self, account_id: &str, node: FileNode) {
    let mut guard = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
    if let Some(store) = guard.accounts.get_mut(account_id) {
        store.nodes.insert(node.id.clone(), node);
    }
}
```

The doc notes only that state is not bumped. Several other
invariant violations go unmentioned:

1. **Dangling `parent_id`.** A seeded node may reference a parent
   that does not exist in the store. `get_ancestors` will silently
   truncate the chain when it hits the missing id (memory.rs:604
   `if let Some(node) = store.nodes.get(&parent_id)` — the walk just
   stops). Downstream impacts: a `fetchParents` query against a
   dangling-parent fixture returns a partial parent chain that the
   client cannot distinguish from "this node IS at the root".

2. **Silently-dropped seeding for unknown account.** The `if let
   Some(store) = ...` branch makes the call a no-op when
   `account_id` was not registered first. The function returns `()`
   — the caller cannot tell whether the seed succeeded or was
   discarded. A test that calls `seed_node` before `with_account`
   produces a passing-but-empty backend; a regression in test setup
   is invisible.

3. **Duplicate-id overwrite.** `HashMap::insert` replaces; a test
   that seeds two nodes with the same id silently keeps the second.
   Sibling-test reuse can produce ghost cleanups.

4. **No cycle check.** A test that seeds A with parent=B and B with
   parent=A will produce infinite-loop behaviour on `get_ancestors`.
   The actual `get_ancestors` impl uses a `visited` set so the loop
   terminates, but the result is "every node in the cycle is its own
   ancestor" — a wrong-shape ancestor chain. The cycle case for
   `seed_node` should at minimum be documented as the caller's
   responsibility to avoid.

Why this is `api-contract,underspecified` rather than just a docs
gap: the function is the documented seam for "downstream contributors
to study and for smoke tests / examples" per the module-level doc.
A contributor copying this pattern into a real backend will copy
the no-validation semantics by default and ship a backend that
accepts inconsistent data.

Suggested fix:

- Either validate in `seed_node` (reject dangling parent, reject
  duplicate id, reject cycles) and return `Result<(), MemoryError>`.
- Or rename to `unchecked_seed_node` and document the four
  invariants above as caller-managed preconditions.

Propagation note: canonical sibling does not have a comparable
seed-node helper; the closest analogues are
`MemoryBackend::store_blob` (memory.rs:262-266 in mail-server, no
validation) and the per-domain seeding done through full handler
calls. Mail-server's `store_blob` has the same "silently drop on
unknown account" foot-gun but for blobs. Filing the propagation
context as a hint, not a hard ask — the fix can be local first.

`api-contract,underspecified` because the seed semantics shape what
"a valid backend state" means, and four classes of invalid state
slip through silently.
title: MemoryBackend::seed_node accepts dangling parent_id with no validation, breaks tree invariants silently
